notes.text: Listen — God turns his speech to the Gentiles, and invites them to hearken to those counsels and doctrines which the Jews would reject. Me - Unto Christ: Isaiah speaks these words in the name of Christ.

A sword — As he made me the great teacher of his church, so he made my word, quick and powerful, and sharper than any two- edged sword. Hath he hid - He will protect me from all mine enemies. Made me - Like an arrow, whose point is bright and polished; which therefore pierceth deeper.

O Israel — As the name of David is sometimes given to his successors, so here the name of Israel may not unfitly be given to Christ, not only because he descended from his loins; but also because he was the true and the great Israel, who, in a more eminent manner, prevailed with God, as that name signifies, of whom Jacob, who was first called Israel, was but a type.

Then said I — Lord, thou sayest thou wilt be glorified by my ministry; but I find it otherwise. In vain - Without any considerable fruit of my word and works among the Israelites. My judgment - My right, the reward which by his promise, and my purchase, is my right.

To bring — To convert the apostate Israelites to God. Not gathered - Not brought home to God by my ministry. Yet - God will not despise me for the unsuccessfulness of my labours, but will honour and glorify me. My strength - To support and strengthen me under this and all other discouragements.

He — The Lord. It is - This is but a small favour. The tribes - That remnant of them which shall survive all their calamities. My salvation - The great instrument and author of that eternal salvation which I will give to the Gentiles.

His Holy One — The Holy One of Israel. To him - To Christ, to whom, in the days of his flesh, this description fully agrees: for men, both Jews and Gentiles among whom he lived, did despise him from their hearts; and the nation, of which he was a member, abhorred both his person and his doctrine; and he was so far from being a temporal monarch, that he came in the form of a servant, and was a servant of rulers, professing subjection and paying tribute unto Caesar. Kings - Though for a time thou shalt be despised, yet after a while thou shalt be advanced to such glory, that kings shall look upon thee with reverence. Arise - From their seats to worship thee. Faithful - Because God shall make good his promises to thee. Chuse thee - And although thou shalt be rejected by thine own people, yet God will manifest to the world, that thou, and thou only, art the person whom he hath chosen to be the Redeemer of mankind.

glossa.text: *Hear, ye islands.* ((HIER.)) After the calling of the remnant of Israel and the objection of the unbelieving (concerning whom, *There is no peace to the wicked, saith the Lord* ), under the name of the islands he addresses, in the person of the Son, the Churches from among the Gentiles.
*A sharp sword. I came not to send peace, but the sword ((Matth. X))*, separating, that is, the evil from the good.
*I will be glorified.* Which he was not in the other servants: *Father, I have glorified thy name ((Joan. XVII.))* And elsewhere: *Arise, my glory ((Psal. LVI))*, etc.

*And I said.* ((ID.)) As though he said: How have I glorified thee, I who could not call back to thee a great part of the Jews? But here man's free choice is shown: for it is God's to call, ours to believe, yet with him helping, that the just may obtain the reward of their will.

*Therefore my judgment,* etc. ((ID.)) The Father shall judge whether I have done for them all the things I owed: *I have manifested thy name to the men whom thou gavest me.* And elsewhere: *I have glorified thee upon the earth ((Joan. XVII))*.

*My work.* Others: My labour and my sorrow: because he wept over the city, and said in the Psalm: *What profit is there in my blood? ((Psal. XXIX.))* According to the Hebrew, hanging on the cross far from my salvation are the words of my lamentations.
*Glorified.* As though he said: I have lost the Jews, but I am glorified among the Gentiles, whence, *All power is given to me in heaven and in earth. ((Matth. XXVIII))*.

*Abhorred.* Christ and his Nazarenes, whom the Jews daily curse in their synagogues, because on their account they lost their kingdom, their place and their nation.

*Kings.* The prophet to the Son. *Kings shall see* thee coming to judgment: *Kings,* namely the apostles and the others who shall judge with the Lord.

notes.text: A wonder — For my many and sore calamities.

glossa.text:
*Unto the end.* ((AUG.)) Concerning the commendation of grace, etc., *as far as* grace is commended in almost every single syllable.

*Of the sons of Jonadab.* ((ID.)) To sons that are willing, etc., *as far as* who of themselves are evil.

((CAS.)) Or thus: we are admonished in the title to have the devotion of the sons of Jonadab, etc., *as far as* but they, by their accustomed malice, remained in obstinacy.

*In thee, O Lord, have I hoped.* The just man in general speaks, from the beginning of the world unto its end: placing all his hope in God, he commends his grace, lest we presume upon false things in ourselves.

((CAS.)) Or, the former captives are in the world, from which one can escape: the second in hell. Or, *of the former,* that is, of those who were taken by vices before they became sons of Christ. This whole psalm commends with the utmost earnestness the grace of God, which is given freely.
*Be thou unto me a God, a protector, and a place of strength,* etc. Two things he promised, two others he renders.
*Of the sinner.* ((AUG.)) There are two kinds of sinners: some received the law, as the Jews and the Christians; others did not, as the pagans.

*From my youth.* ((CAS.)) That is, from my conversion, or from the time when I began to fight against the devil. ((AUG.)) *From my youth,* from the time when I began to hope in thee, etc., *as far as* a young man fights, but falls, unless God be his hope.

*In thee is my song.* ((CAS.)) It is a delight to me to be in thee. *Always.* That the benefits may be unbroken. *Always.* ((AUG.)) Both in the present, etc., *as far as* against which nothing stands.

*Let my mouth be filled.* ((CAS.)) He has told the benefits; now he asks that he may be able to give thanks. For if God does not fill the mouth, desire does not burn. *All the day thy greatness.* ((AUG.)) That is, without intermission, etc., *as far as* under the name of greatness therefore he includes all things.

*Cast me not off.* ((CAS.)) Concerning the grace to be given in the time of old age and of decrepitude. *Of old age.* ((AUG.)) Old age was in Christ, when he was made a wonder, when he was made weak upon the cross and mocked; and it is called old age because he took it on from oldness, whence: *Our old man is crucified with him ((Rom. VI))*.

*For my enemies have said.* ((AUG.)) This is said of Christ, who among the hands of his enemies was made weak, and, once seized, as though he could do nothing. But here this is said of his members, because he had such things also from our person.

*God hath forsaken him.* ((AUG.)) Whence elsewhere: *Why hast thou forsaken me?* that is, why do they think me forsaken, to their own hurt. *For if they had known it, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory.*
*Depart not from me.* ((CAS.)) They think him far off while he delays; *depart not,* that he may expose [them] to graver things .

*Let them be confounded,* etc. ((CAS.)) Because the things ordained of God are not changed. *That detract my soul.* Otherwise, that set my soul at strife. ((AUG.)) That is, provoking us to resist God, which is to wage war against God; as those do to whom God is not pleasing in their adversities, which is to hold him unjust. The soul is also set at strife if it hates those from whom it suffers. *That seek.* ((ID.)) As Job's wife did, who said: *Say somewhat against God, and die ((Job. VII))*. As also Tobias's wife says: *Where are thy justices? ((Tob. IV, 2.))* She said this that God might be displeasing to him.

*And I will add.* ((AUG.)) The addition of praise is, after the creation of all things, the praise concerning the incarnation and the resurrection, which the lines below teach. *All.* ((AUG.)) Because, though he be praised in all other things, not yet in this, that he raised up our flesh unto the eternal way *viam*; read *vitam*, "life", which is the praise added for the resurrection of Christ. Or, all praise would be there, and nothing would be lacking to praise, if he condemned sinners, because it would be justice; but because thou deliverest even these: *I will add above all thy praise.*

notes.text: To them that perish — By obstinately rejecting the only name whereby they can be saved. But to us who are saved - Now saved from our sins, and in the way to everlasting salvation, it is the great instrument of the power of God.
For it is written — And the words are remarkably applicable to this great event. Isaiah xxix, 14

Where is the wise? &c. — The deliverance of Judea from Sennacherib is what Isaiah refers to in these words; in a bold and beautiful allusion to which, the apostle in the clause that follows triumphs over all the opposition of human wisdom to the victorious gospel of Christ. What could the wise men of the gentiles do against this? or the Jewish scribes? or the disputers of this world? - Those among both, who, proud of their acuteness, were fond of controversy, and thought they could confute all opponents. Hath not God made foolish the wisdom of this world - That is, shown it to be very foolishness. Isaiah xxxiii, 18

For since in the wisdom of God — According to his wise disposals, leaving them to make the trial. The world - Whether Jewish or gentile, by all its boasted wisdom knew not God - Though the whole creation declared its Creator, and though he declared himself by all the prophets; it pleased God, by a way which those who perish count mere foolishness, to save them that believe.

For whereas the Jews demand of the apostles, as they did of their Lord, more signs still, after all they have seen already; and the Greeks, or gentiles, seek wisdom — The depths of philosophy, and the charms of eloquence.

We go on to preach, in a plain and historical, not rhetorical or philosophical, manner, Christ crucified, to the Jews a stumblingblock — Just opposite to the "signs" they demand. And to the Greeks foolishness - A silly tale, just opposite to the wisdom they seek.

But to them that are called — And obey the heavenly calling. Christ - With his cross, his death, his life, his kingdom. And they experience, first, that he is the power, then, that he is the wisdom, of God.
Because the foolishness of God — The gospel scheme, which the world judge to be mere foolishness, is wiser than the wisdom of men; and, weak as they account it, stronger than all the strength of men.
Behold your calling — What manner of men they are whom God calls. That not many wise men after the flesh - In the account of the world. Not many mighty - Men of power and authority.
Things that are not — The Jews frequently called the gentiles, "Them that are not," 2 Esdras vi. 56, 57. In so supreme contempt did they hold them. The things that are - In high esteem.
That no flesh — A fit appellation. Flesh is fair, but withering as grass. May glory before God - In God we ought to glory.

Of him — Out of his free grace and mercy. Are ye Engrafted into Christ Jesus, who is made unto us that believe wisdom, who were before utterly foolish and ignorant. Righteousness - The sole ground of our justification, who were before under the wrath and curse of God. Sanctification - A principle of universal holiness, whereas before we were altogether dead in sin. And redemption - That is, complete deliverance from all evil, and eternal bliss both of soul and body.
Let him glory in the Lord — Not in himself, not in the flesh, not in the world. Jer. ix, 23, 24

glossa.text:
*To them that perish.* That is, to the wise men of the world, whose wisdom both perishes and is shown to be false, and who themselves are to be damned.

*The power of God.* In that, being slain, he conquered the devil and set man free, or he gives power to believers, by which miracles are done, when the matter requires.

*For it is written.* Therefore he did not send me in wisdom, because he had foretold that he would not receive it into the preaching of the gospel, but would destroy it and reject it from the college of his preachers: and so it was done.

*It pleased God, by the foolishness of preaching, to save them that believe.* That is, that by the faith of the cross eternity should come to mortals: that salvation might be found there, where foolishness is believed.

*For see.* Truly the foolish and weak thing of God is wiser and stronger than men. Which you can prove in yourselves. For unwise and weak men called you, among the foolish and weak things of God such callers are numbered, who nevertheless confound the wise and the strong. And truly they are such, *for there are not many wise.* But he does not say, *none,* perhaps on his own account, who alone among the apostles was skilled in secular letters, rich in earthly goods, and conspicuous by kindred of Roman rank; who nevertheless counted these things as nothing, and did not use them.

*But the foolish things.* Behold, they act openly against the ordinance of God, because they boast the wisdom of the world, while God sets forth humility. For God came humble, seeking the humble, not the lofty. And although he first chose the poor, the unlearned, the weak, yet he does not leave the wise, the rich, the noble, but if he were to choose these first, they would seem to themselves to be chosen for the merit of such things; and so there would be in them the pride by which man fell. Unless the fisherman had gone faithfully before, the humble orator would not have followed. Whence Nathanael, a learned man, was not chosen for an apostle.
*That no flesh may glory.* Of itself, but of God, which is shown there: he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord.
*But of him.* Let no one glory of himself, but yet there is another glory, because of him you are.

notes.text: Certain Greeks — A prelude of the Gentile Church. That these were circumcised does not appear. But they came up on purpose to worship the God of Israel.

These came to Philip of Bethsaida in Galilee — Perhaps they used to lodge there, in their journey to Jerusalem. Or they might believe, a Galilean would be more ready to serve them herein, than a Jew. Sir - They spake to him, as to one they were little acquainted with. We would see Jesus - A modest request. They could scarce expect that he would now have time to talk with them.
The hour is come that the Son of man should be glorified — With the Father and in the sight of every creature. But he must suffer first.

Unless a grain of wheat die — The late resurrection of Lazarus gave our Lord a natural occasion of speaking on this subject. And agreeable to his infinite knowledge, he singles out, from among so many thousands of seeds, almost the only one that dies in the earth: and which therefore was an exceeding proper similitude, peculiarly adapted to the purpose for which he uses it. The like is not to be found in any other grain, except millet, and the large bean.
He that loveth his life — More than the will of God; shall lose it eternally: and he that hateth his life - In comparison of the will of God, shall preserve it. Matt. x, 39.
Let him follow me — By hating his life: and where I am - In heaven. If any man serve me - Thus, him will the Father honour.

Now is my soul troubled — He had various foretastes of his passion. And what shall I say? - Not what shall I choose? For his heart was fixed in choosing the will of his Father: but he laboured for utterance. The two following clauses, Save me from this hour - For this cause I came - Into the world; for the sake of this hour (of suffering) seem to have glanced through his mind in one moment. But human language could not so express it.
Father, glorify thy name — Whatever I suffer. Now the trouble was over. I have glorified it - By thy entrance into this hour. And I will glorify it - By thy passing through it.

The multitude who stood and heard — A sound, but not the distinct words - In the most glorious Revelations there may remain something obscure, to exercise our faith. Said, It thundered -Thunder did frequently attend a voice from heaven. Perhaps it did so now.

Now — This moment. And from this moment Christ thirsted more than ever, till his baptism was accomplished. Is the judgment of this world - That is, now is the judgment given concerning it, whose it shall be. Now shall the prince of this world - Satan, who had gained possession of it by sin and death, be cast out -That is, judged, condemned, cast out of his possession, and out of the bounds of Christ's kingdom.

Lifted up from the earth — This is a Hebraism which signifies dying. Death in general is all that is usually imported. But our Lord made use of this phrase, rather than others that were equivalent, because it so well suited the particular manner of his death. I will draw all men - Gentiles as well as Jews. And those who follow my drawings, Satan shall not be able to keep.
How sayest thou, The Son of man must be lifted up? — How can these things be reconciled? Very easily. He first dies, and then abideth forever. Who is this Son of man? - Is he the Christ? Psalm cx, 4.
Then Jesus said to them — Not answering them directly, but exhorting them to improve what they had heard already. The light - I and my doctrine.
The children of light — The children of God, wise, holy, happy.

glossa.text: *These therefore came.* He shows the Gentiles converted through the preaching of the apostles.

*But Jesus.* They were of the Jews who cried out: *Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord;* now the Gentiles seek to see him: behold, two walls meeting. And so the corner stone speaks. *The hour is come that should be glorified.* This is not a glorification concerning those who wish to see him, but on their occasion he announces the coming fulness of the Gentiles, when he has been glorified in heaven. But this height of glorification is preceded by the lowliness of the passion; whence: *Amen, amen I say to you,* etc. Where he calls himself the grain which must be mortified and multiplied; to which passion, having now exhorted them, he adds: *He that loveth his life,* etc.

*Unless the grain of wheat. ((AUG.))* He himself is the wheat by which the faithful soul ought to live. The grain, from which the spiritual harvest ought to rise. Though there be many grains of seeds, he compares himself to none but wheat; whence the custom began in the Church that of this grain alone the body of the Lord is confected.

*He that loveth. ((AUG.))* He who loves in this life loses in the life to come what is more fitting; whence he adds: *He that hateth his life,* etc. He does not love but hates his life in this world who, loving God, chooses rather to be slain than to sin against him.

*If any man minister to me.* The price of the work by which he is ministered to is to be with him, without whom it is nowhere good to be, and with whom it is nowhere ill to be; whence he adds more openly, *if any man minister to me.*

*Now my soul is troubled. And what shall I say?* The passion having been foretold, and the exhortation to it set beneath it, as though the voice of his own fortitude had been given, he adds the affection of our infirmity, which he truly took upon himself, but of his will, for us, lest we despair of this infirmity: in which also he teaches what we ought to say, and whither to flee. As if he should say: My soul is troubled; what shall I say? whither shall I flee? whom shall I call upon? in whom shall I hope? In the Father who saves, to whom I set forth my will, because for this cause, that I might suffer these things, I came unto this hour; whence also my glorification comes about thus, and in my members.
*Father, glorify.* I seek salvation, but I do not refuse the passion; for which passion glorify me, which is the glory of thy name.
*This voice came not because of me.* He shows that this voice did not declare to him what he knew, but to those to whom it had to be declared.

*Now is the judgment.* Of discernment, namely, which is before the last judgment of damnation, because now, through the passion, the right of the devil being destroyed, many shall be set free; whence, expounding it, he subjoins: I suffer, I am troubled, and through these things, etc. *He shall be cast out.* He shall be driven out from the redeemed; when the apostles preach he shall be fully driven out, who of old by few, even though a man be tempted without, does not hurt within.

*And how sayest thou,* etc. How shall he die upon the cross? For they thought that he had said this which they were plotting to do. The Son of man. Because they held this in memory, that he had often said that he was the Son of man, not that he had said it here, *if the Son of man shall be lifted up. Who is this Son of man?* For if he is Christ, he abides for ever. If he abides for ever, how shall he be lifted up from the earth, that is, die upon the cross?

*Walk.* That is, understand the whole: both that Christ was to die that he might redeem, and that he was to live for ever in heaven, whither he may lead you. Or, while you have Christ with you, lest the darkness of ignorance and of everlasting death seize upon you. *He knoweth not whither he goeth.* He who does not believe the death of Christ knows not whither he goes, but stumbles upon the rock of scandal, which is Christ, while the Jews despise and mock him as dead.

*Whilst you have the light.* That is, while you understand something of the truth concerning the eternity of Christ, believe in the truth, adding what belongs to his lowliness, that you may be born again in the truth. *From them.* Not from those who had begun to believe, but from those who envied him. That he hid himself, he took counsel for our infirmity; he did not derogate from his own power.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Sir, we wish to see Jesus.
The hour has come for him to be glorified.
Unless a grain of wheat falls and dies, it stays alone.
If it dies, it bears much fruit.
Walk while you have the light, he says.
Lest the darkness overtake you.
Come, children of light, and worship.
We follow the servant to the cross. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Some came up to the festival asking the question that is still ours: Sir, we wish to see Jesus.
We follow the servant to the cross.
He answers with a seed: unless the grain falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone.
We follow the servant to the cross.
The Lord called his servant from the womb to be a light to the nations, to the end of the earth.
We follow the servant to the cross.
Walk while you have the light, he says, before the night comes; believe, and become children of light.
We follow the servant to the cross.
So come to the light that is fading toward Friday, and worship while it shines.
We follow the servant to the cross. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Sir, we wish to see Jesus.

Here is the servant of God.
Walk while you still have the light.
Here is the servant of God.
Come, children of light, and worship.
Here is the servant of God. Amen.
